statement: In triangle ABC, three segments join A to points on side BC, and one segment parallel to BC joins the other two sides, crossing all three of those segments, as shown. How many triangles of any size can be found in the figure?

figure.alt: Triangle ABC with A at the top. Three segments run from A down to points on side BC, making five lines through A including AB and AC. A segment parallel to BC, about halfway down, joins AB to AC and crosses all three inner segments.

choices.misconception: I counted only the four smallest triangles at the top of the figure.
I counted the eight smallest pieces, but the four below the parallel segment have four sides, not three.
I counted only the triangles that rest on BC and forgot the ones that rest on the parallel segment.
I also counted the 10 four-sided shapes between the parallel segment and BC, as if they were triangles.

hints: Every triangle here has A as one corner.
A triangle in this figure needs two of the lines through A and one of the two crosswise lines. Count the pairs of lines through A, then decide how many crosswise lines each pair can close off.
There are 5 lines through A: AB, AC and the three inner segments. Any two of them, closed by BC, make a triangle.

solutions.reliable: The lines through A are AB, AC and the three inner segments: 5 lines, giving 5 x 4 / 2 = 10 pairs. Each pair, together with BC, makes a triangle, and each pair, together with the parallel segment, makes another. No triangle avoids A, because the two crosswise lines are parallel and cannot both be sides. So there are 10 + 10 = 20 triangles. The transferable idea: describe a hidden shape by the lines that form it, then count choices of lines rather than looking for pictures.
solutions.elegant: Along BC the four small triangles at A combine into 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 10 triangles, and the same happens along the parallel segment, giving 20.

whyOnTest: Hidden-figure counts at this level need a system, and naming each triangle by its lines is the system that avoids missing a layer.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
